note: Each finding shown is held by a strict xfail test named in 'test'. 'cases' are the keys of twice.json the finding rests on. 'ruling' is empty where no decision is in question.

findings.claim: A second identical Approach (what the code calls no new decision) writes a second IRB-override record and a second console.approach_override event: the override trail overcounts.
findings.expected: One override per decision. The mark rows are append-only by design (D-104, docs data dictionary), so they are not the defect; home.py:1253 (D-989, D-1152) says an Approach on an Approach of the same list is no new decision.

findings.claim: A second identical save of the withdrawal (also enrolment, consent, an SAE form) form changes nothing but answers 'Saved.' and writes a data_entry event with changed 0.
findings.expected: The second person is told plainly that nothing changed; no written rule; expected by the card.

findings.claim: Two 'send now' at once send each person's patient digest (N1, N2) twice: the once-a-day check, the send and the log are not one step.
findings.expected: One digest per person and day (notify.py:371; tests/console/test_health_mail.py:129 'once a day').

findings.claim: Disabling an account that is already disabled writes a second 'disable' audit event with the same Undo toast; a reset sent twice resets twice (two console.user events).
findings.expected: One disable event; the second answer says the account is already off; no written rule; expected by the card.

findings.claim: The enrolment form replayed after a withdrawal is refused as 'correct the 1 marked fields' (a change reason), not as 'the participant is withdrawn'.
findings.expected: A plain refusal naming the withdrawal; no written rule; expected by the card. Not run: whether a reason given then changes the enrolment date of a withdrawn participant.

findings.claim: Calling the timer's entry (scheduler._submit) twice makes two INGEST jobs. The timer itself is one in-memory APScheduler job (id 'ingest', coalesce, max_instances=1), so it was not shown to fire twice; two orchestrator processes on one job store would each have that timer (not run).
findings.expected: One ingest per night; D-492 (M1) keys one run per study and night for the chain only; no written rule for the ingest.

findings.claim: Two retries of one failed scheduler job at once (POST /jobs/{job_id}/retry, two clients) make two jobs: the 'one already queued' read and the new job are not one step. Hypothesis: the same holds for a list job (two candidate lists).
findings.expected: One new job, the other refused (D-474; core.py:404-406 refuses a retry while one is queued or running).

findings.claim: A double click on break-glass open (the CSRF token is fixed for the session, auth.py:762 per the review) makes two grants: two console.breakglass_open events, two notices to the PI and the steward; the second ends the first.
findings.expected: One grant per request; no written rule; expected by the card.

findings.claim: A second identical opt-out answers done=same but writes a second console.opt_out event that names what it removed, with nothing marking it a no-op.
findings.expected: One event, or the second marked as no change; no written rule; same pattern as V11-04.

findings.claim: An Approach replayed after the study is closed is accepted (303): a new mark row and a new screening number on a closed study.
findings.expected: D-386: closed is final and a close ends recruitment.
findings.ruling: D-386 has no rule for marks

findings.claim: Ending a break-glass grant that is already ended writes a second console.breakglass_end event; switching EDC prefill on when it is on writes a second edc.switch event and switch record.
findings.expected: One event per change; no written rule; same pattern as V11-04.

findings.claim: A double submit of /pilot/request, /pilot/case, /pilot/consent or /pilot/jobs/{id}/release sends a second job request (a second console.request event and JobCreate at the stand-in). Whether the real orchestrator then makes two jobs was not run.
findings.place: services/console/app.py:1946, app.py:2138, app.py:2079, app.py:1583 (the pilot forms)
findings.expected: One job per submit; no written rule; expected by the card.

findings.claim: After the person opts out, the coordinator's earlier consent and enrolment forms are saved: 2 steps and 5 values written, the participant becomes enrolled.
findings.expected: The EDC path refuses an opted-out person (services/edc/service.py:129-132); D-273 and D-441 name the readers, not the data-entry form.
findings.ruling: no decision says whether data entry is refused after an opt-out

findings.claim: A second acknowledgement of the same SAE by the investigator (a double click) answers 303 and writes a second console.sae_ack and a second life.sae_ack event: the SAE trail shows two acknowledgements.
findings.expected: One acknowledgement per SAE; no written rule; expected by the card (an SAE is a regulated record).
